name: amo-skill
description: Agent workflow skills for design, implementation, review, and documentation.

plugins.name: amo-feature
plugins.description: Use when the user asks how to design or implement a new feature, capability, workflow, page, API, or behavior before coding. Do not use for bug fixes, intentional changes to existing behavior, pure refactors, or second-pass solution challenges.

plugins.name: amo-improve
plugins.description: Use when the user asks how to improve, extend, adjust, or redesign an existing feature or behavior before coding. Do not use for brand-new features, broken behavior, pure refactors, or second-pass solution challenges.

plugins.name: amo-fix
plugins.description: Use when the user asks why existing behavior is broken, incorrect, flaky, regressed, unexpected, or runtime/build behavior is failing and wants a bug-fix approach before coding. Do not use for planned feature changes, pure refactors, or second-pass solution challenges.

plugins.name: amo-refactor
plugins.description: Use when the user asks how to refactor, split modules, clarify architecture, move ownership, reduce coupling, or fix unclear state, data-flow, or component boundaries before coding. Do not use for ordinary feature work, bug fixes, or second-pass solution challenges.

plugins.name: amo-best
plugins.description: Use when the user challenges an existing proposal, asks whether it is the best solution, asks for a better approach, or wants second-pass review of the chosen best-standard, tradeoffs, scope, compatibility, risk, or refactor depth before implementation.

plugins.name: amo-research
plugins.description: Use when the user asks to research how competitor products, communities, or open-source projects implement a feature, find mature reusable approaches, or verify implementation alternatives with external evidence to support solution decisions. Do not use for general market analysis or solution design without external implementation research.

plugins.name: amo-detail
plugins.description: Use when the user asks to understand an existing proposal's overall flow, impact scope, frontend changes, backend data flow, storage, or scheduled tasks. Focus on presenting proposal details, not initial solution design, challenges to the chosen approach, direct implementation, or code review.

plugins.name: amo-implement
plugins.description: Use when the user asks to implement an already defined proposal and verify the result, keeping changes focused, comments useful, and frontend content free of conversation or implementation notes. Do not use for solution design, proposal explanation, or standalone code review.

plugins.name: amo-review
plugins.description: Use when the user asks to review implemented code for code style, redundancy, unnecessary abstractions, wrappers, helpers, adapters, parsers, type guards, TypeScript type noise, or composable usage clarity.

plugins.name: amo-draft
plugins.description: Use when the user asks to write or edit development-time content, website or page copy, requirement notes, implementation docs, version notes, release notes, or temporary project documentation, especially when reference material, examples, chat history, or implementation process could pollute the target artifact.
